title: Evaluating the Efficacy of a "Quiet Knee Protocol" in Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty (TKA): A Prospective Randomized Study
official: Evaluating the Efficacy of a "Quiet Knee Protocol" in Primary Total Knee Arthroplasty (TKA): A Prospective Randomized Study
summary:
The goal of this randomized clinical trial is to access the following:

1. Compare the effectiveness of the QKP versus a standard rehabilitation protocol in improving postoperative pain control, ROM, and functional recovery following primary TKA.
2. Assess whether the QKP reduces reliance on formal PT services.
3. Evaluate the impact of QKP on secondary outcomes, including opioid consumption, manipulation under anesthesia (MUA) rates, and patient satisfaction scores.

Patients will be randomized into either a standard of care arm vs QKP rehabilitation protocol arm. Each group will answer questionnaires and be followed for 12 months.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults (≥18 years) undergoing unilateral primary TKA for osteoarthritis
* Willingness to adhere to the assigned rehabilitation protocol
* Ability to provide informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Revision TKA or bilateral procedures
* Preexisting neuromuscular disorders affecting mobility
* Prior knee surgery within 12 months
* No Joint Hardware
* Agree to avoid plane trips post-surgery for 2 weeks
* Patients with 100-degree flexion contracture
* Pregnant subjects
